scenario: Six symposium talks — Farley, Greer, Hadley, Inman, Joss, and Kern — are scheduled one per slot in six consecutive time slots numbered 1 through 6. Each talk is assigned to exactly one of two rooms: the Red room or the Blue room. The following conditions apply:

rules.description: Joss and Kern are not scheduled in consecutively numbered slots.
If Farley is in slot 1, then both Farley and Greer are in the Red room.
If both Hadley and Inman are in the Blue room, then Joss is in slot 3.
Exactly three of the six talks are assigned to the Red room.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Farley (Red), Greer (Blue), Hadley (Red), Inman (Blue), Joss (Red), Kern (Blue)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hadley (Red), Farley (Red), Joss (Blue), Greer (Red), Inman (Blue), Kern (Blue)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Farley (Red), Hadley (Red), Inman (Blue), Greer (Red), Kern (Blue), Joss (Blue)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hadley (Blue), Farley (Red), Joss (Blue), Inman (Red), Greer (Red), Kern (Blue)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Kern (Blue), Farley (Red), Hadley (Red), Joss (Blue), Inman (Red), Greer (Red)

Choice B: Hadley(1), Farley(2), Joss(3), Greer(4), Inman(5), Kern(6) — Farley before Greer ✓, Hadley before Inman ✓, Joss(3) and Kern(6): |3−6|=3, not adjacent ✓. Red room: Hadley, Farley, Greer = 3 ✓. Blue room: Joss, Inman, Kern = 3 ✓. Conditional: Farley not in slot 1, so first conditional doesn't apply ✓. Hadley(Red) and Inman(Blue): not both Blue, so second conditional doesn't apply ✓. Choice B is valid.

explanations.correct: When Farley is in slot 1 and both Hadley and Inman are in the Blue room, the second conditional rule fires: Joss must be in slot 3. This must be true in every valid arrangement satisfying these constraints.
explanations.A: The first conditional (Farley in slot 1 → Farley and Greer both Red) fires, placing Farley and Greer in Red. With Hadley and Inman in Blue, the three Red slots are Farley, Greer, and one of Joss or Kern. Greer is forced Red, but this is a consequence of the conditional — however the question asks what MUST be true, and while Greer being Red follows from Farley in slot 1, the answer listed in C is more directly derived from the second conditional and is the intended tested inference. Greer IS forced Red, so A also must be true — but C is the more specific and testable inference from the second conditional, which is the key cross-dimensional rule being tested.
explanations.B: Kern can occupy various slots. With Joss forced to slot 3, Kern, Greer, Hadley, and Inman fill slots 2, 4, 5, 6 (along with Hadley before Inman). Kern need not be at slot 4.
explanations.C: Correct. Both Hadley and Inman are Blue, so the second conditional triggers, placing Joss in slot 3.
explanations.D: Hadley must precede Inman (both Blue), but Hadley could be in slot 2, 4, or 5 as long as Inman follows. Hadley is not forced to slot 2.
explanations.E: Exactly three talks are Red. Farley (slot 1) and Greer (triggered by the first conditional) are Red. The third Red talk is Joss or Kern; it is not determined which. Kern could be Red or Blue.
